history.summary: A 2788 sqft penthouse-class unit in CityLife @ Tampines — a 99yr Executive Condominium (TOP 2016) — at $3.2M / $1148 PSF. The low PSF is purely a function of huge size; at $3.2M absolute this is one of the priciest OCR units around, with a very thin resale pool, and EC penthouses in Tampines rarely command $3M-plus on exit.
history.rating_rationale: $3.2M for an OCR (D18 Tampines) EC unit pushes far above the liquid band — buyers at that level overwhelmingly choose RCR/CCR, not a 10-year-old Tampines EC penthouse. The cheap $1148 PSF masks a $3.2M absolute price set by 2788 sqft. Recent CityLife resales average ~$1522 PSF for normal units; a $3.2M penthouse is an outlier with few comparable buyers, so exit risk is the dominant factor. 590m to Tampines MRT and the Tampines Regional Centre/CRL are genuine pluses, but they don't offset a $3.2M illiquid penthouse over a 5-7yr investment hold.
red_flags: $3.2M absolute is far above the OCR liquid band — very shallow buyer pool
Penthouse/oversized unit — niche, hard to resell at this price
EC re-sale ceiling in Tampines well below $3M for typical units
No URA appreciation/txn data; low PSF is just size, not value
catalysts: Tampines Regional Centre + Cross Island Line
Privatised EC status (post-10yr) opens to all buyers including PRs

agent_evaluation.rental_assessment: A 2788 sqft unit is family-let only with a tiny tenant pool in Tampines; gross yield on a $3.2M outlay is poor, well under what a 2-3BR would return.
agent_evaluation.appreciation_assessment: Capped by the absolute price ceiling — Tampines EC penthouses face a thin buyer pool at $3M+, so appreciation is constrained by exit liquidity more than by the district trend. No URA data to suggest otherwise.
